extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying to the HHMI Investigator Program / prospective HHMI Investigators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility/selection criteria for scientists applying to the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Investigator Program, including application components, institutional and professional requirements, and the attributes HHMI seeks in Investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: People-focused selection (selects people, not projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI supports people, rather than projects, because it’s individual scientists who break barriers to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI selects investigators who 'ask tough questions in science, even at the risk of failure.' Preferred candidates develop new tools and methods, forge links between biology and medicine, and are committed to mentoring and training the next generation of scientists. Emphasis is on scientific creativity, innovation, and potential for high-impact discovery rather than narrowly defined project plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required terminal degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD and/or MD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible host institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must plan to perform research at one of over 200 eligible U.S. institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI Investigators are based at eligible universities, colleges, and other research institutions across the United States; appointment involves a collaborative agreement with the investigator’s host institution where the researcher holds a concurrent appointment and research is performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment / position requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a position that represents substantial commitment by their institution, such as a tenure-track faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The position should enable the candidate to direct a research team and create a lab environment well suited to tackling profound science questions; appointments involve collaborative agreements with host institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of peer-reviewed funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a track record of peer-reviewed funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This demonstrates the candidate’s ability to obtain competitive support and sustain a research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-training professional experience requirement (competition-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines a required length of post-training, professional experience prior to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the experience window specified in the specific competition announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific discipline scope (competition-defined)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines the breadth of scientific disciplines to be considered; however, most competitions are open to most biological and biomedical disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the specific competition announcement to confirm eligibility of particular fields or interdisciplinary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: five highlighted research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requirements include five highlighted research articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should select five publications that best showcase their most significant contributions and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: summary of major research contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include a summary of your major research contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should contextualize the five highlighted articles and explain the applicant’s key scientific achievements and their significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: program description of ongoing and planned research
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requires a program description focused on your ongoing and planned research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because HHMI funds people rather than projects, the program description should convey the applicant’s vision, scientific trajectory, and the broader questions they intend to pursue with HHMI support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of investigators is made by HHMI scientific leadership and is based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI uses external panels of distinguished scientists to assess candidates; review emphasizes the qualities HHMI values (innovation, leadership, potential for major discovery). Applicants should be evaluated on both past achievements and future potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment term and renewal assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHMI investigator appointment has a seven-year renewable term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal decisions are made by HHMI scientific leadership, based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards. Renewal likely considers continued scientific excellence, productivity, and alignment with HHMI’s mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership, team building, and lab environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators direct a research team and create a lab environment well suited to tackling profound science questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI expects Investigators to lead and mentor, build productive teams, and foster a research environment that enables ambitious, high-risk/high-reward science and training of junior scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of discovery and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI Investigators are widely known for their scientific discoveries, their innovation, and their success in pushing the bounds of knowledge in biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated past impact — including transformative discoveries or novel methods — is a core criterion for selection.
